data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise choosing between adjective and adverb forms and recognising common forms with different meanings.
learningPoints: Use adjectives to describe nouns and after linking verbs.
Use adverbs to modify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs.
Recognise irregular adverbs such as well.
Distinguish pairs such as hard/hardly and late/lately.
Avoid using an adjective where an adverb is required.
Choose the form that matches both grammar and meaning.

sections.summary: Using an adjective after a linking verb.
sections.explain: Use an adjective after FEEL, LOOK, SEEM and similar linking verbs.

words.word: She looks tired today.
She looks tiredly today.
She tired looks today.

sections.summary: Using an adverb to modify an action.
sections.explain: Use an adverb to describe how an action is performed.

words.word: He answered the question correctly.
He answered the question correct.
He correct answered the question.

sections.explain: WELL is the usual adverb corresponding to GOOD.

words.word: She speaks English very well.
She speaks English very good.
She well is speaking English very.

sections.explain: GOOD is an adjective and can follow linking verbs such as FEEL.

words.word: I feel good about the result.
I feel wellly about the result.
I good feel about the result.

sections.explain: HARD means with effort; HARDLY means almost not.

words.word: She works hard every day.
She works hardly every day, meaning with effort.
She hardly works hard every day, meaning the same thing.

sections.explain: HARDLY has a negative-like meaning: almost not.

words.word: I could hardly hear him.
I could hard hear him.
I hardly could hear him loudly.

sections.explain: LATE means after the expected time; LATELY means recently.

words.word: He arrived late for the meeting.
He arrived lately for the meeting.
He late arrived for the meeting.

sections.explain: LATELY means recently and is often used with the Present Perfect.

words.word: I haven't seen her much lately.
I haven't seen her much late.
I lately haven't saw her much.

sections.summary: Using an adjective with a noun.
sections.explain: Adjectives normally come before the nouns they describe.

words.word: It was a surprisingly difficult exam.
It was a surprisingly difficulty exam.
It was a surprise difficultly exam.

sections.summary: Using an adverb to modify an adjective.
sections.explain: An adverb can modify an adjective: EXTREMELY + IMPORTANT.

words.word: This information is extremely important.
This information is extreme important.
This information extremely is importance.
